blocks.text: The exhibition at 2B Galerie presents some thirty photos that are not conventional photographs; they are not the result of intuition or impressions, but of ideas and experiments.

Of Hungarian descent on his father’s side, Alain Fleischer is a French multidisciplinary artist, filmmaker and writer. His work breaks free from the codes of classical photography: his images are the product neither of intuition nor of fleeting impression, but of carefully considered concepts and rigorous experiments. For him, photography is not a fixed work but a malleable material to be shaped.

Alain Fleischer’s photographic work is characterized mainly by experiments with reflections, optical illusions and nocturnal light projections. In the early 1970s, at his first public appearances, he drew the attention of the French photographic world with an innovative technique of dressing his nude models in images projected onto the body (“Corps-écrans”, 1970–1971). In a later series, “La Nuit des visages” (1995), instead of resorting to laboratory montage or digital retouching, he projected slides of female faces at night directly onto a tree trunk or a rock. The shot, taken with a long exposure time, creates a mystical image thanks to moonlight filtered in the background. His photographs of the 1980s show the reflections of people in various everyday metal objects such as a spoon, a teapot or an iron, transforming them into unreal, mysterious faces (“Argenterie et autres reflets”). The use of reflection and movement can be found again in his 1981 series “Miroirs-Tiroirs”. He captures the moment when mirror-lined drawers are opened. The result reveals an image of a movement and a reflection that it would be impossible to see with the naked eye. In the series “Happy Days”, it is the models of old paintings, reflected by mirrors pulled by toys, that are extracted from the paintings to become photographs. The installation entitled “Je ne suis qu’une image”, which transforms sound into image, was conceived in 2017. A sculptural version was erected outdoors, in front of the Conservatoire de musique, place Carmen, in Paris.

The exhibition at 2B Galerie presents to the public works that reveal the unlimited possibilities of photography and open the way to a different visual approach. In addition to some thirty photographs, the exhibition also includes a few short videos, which likewise testify to the diversity of his working processes, to Fleischer’s creativity and to his inexhaustible wealth of ideas.
Alain Fleischer, l’aventurier des expériences 3 November – 20 December 2026 2B Galerie Ráday u. 47 1092 Budapest, Hungary https://2b-org.hu/
